Jamie (oncall): quick heads-up — we're scheduling a preemptive drain of a subset of serving nodes in eu-west1 for a kernel micro-patch. window: Tue 2026-03-24 02:00-03:30 UTC. expected impact: transient 100-300ms tail latency spikes, in-flight requests should failover but some 502s possible. please read below for ops plan.

Priya Rao: ack. i'll cover the first 60m, @Jamie will take handback if anything escalates. link to bridge?

devops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0483. Priority: P2. Pager targets: oncall-sre, infra-ops. bridge: https://zoom.example.com/ops-bridge/INC-2026-0483 (internal-only)

Ava (support): drafting customer-facing blurb. proposal: "We will perform a targeted maintenance in eu-west1 on Tue 24 Mar 02:00-03:30 UTC to deploy a kernel micro-patch. Most customers will see no interruption; a small percentage may experience brief request failures. We will post a status update before and after the window." want signoff before pushing to status.redwood.ai/status

Mateo: small note on rollout — we'll do a rolling drain 1/3 of serving pool at a time with 5m cool-downs between shards. aim to keep concurrency targets. if we see error rate >1% sustained for 5m, pause and rollback to previous node set.

Jamie (oncall): Ops playbook excerpt:
```
# drain command
rdwctl nodes drain --region eu-west1 --pool serving-pool --batch-size 1 --grace-period 120
# check kv cache warmup
rdwctl metrics tail --filter "kv_cache_warmup < 0.8" --region eu-west1
```
Keep an eye on token latency p50/p95 and embed queue length.

Priya Rao: adding monitoring checklist:
- open bridge + paste runbook :white_check_mark:
- start traffic shadowing for first batch :in-progress:
- watch per-tenant errors >0.5% :alarm_clock:
- update status page pre-window and at completion :point_up:

ops-runner: i've queued automated alerts: if p99 latency >1200ms or 502 rate >0.8% for >3m, alert oncall and pause drain.

Ava (support): Draft status page pre-window (internal copy):
"We will be performing targeted infrastructure maintenance in eu-west1 on Tue 24 Mar 02:00-03:30 UTC. During the maintenance window, some requests routed to the affected capacity may experience short-lived failures or latency increases. Our platform will automatically failover to healthy capacity; degradation is expected to be brief. We will update this page when maintenance starts and when it completes."

Jamie (oncall): customer email template (short):
"Hi — we will be performing a brief maintenance in eu-west1 on Tue 24 Mar 02:00-03:30 UTC to improve platform stability. You may see intermittent request errors for <5 minutes. No action required. Contact support if you see persistent issues. — Redwood Inference Ops"

Mateo: suggestion: include recommended retry guidance for customers: exponential backoff starting at 200ms, max 3 retries for idempotent calls. mention streaming sessions may be interrupted.

Priya Rao: timeline and ops cadence:
- 01:40 UTC: final preflight check + status page pre-update
- 01:50 UTC: bridge open, runbook pinned
- 02:00 UTC: start first batch drain (1/3 pool)
- 02:20 UTC: observe metrics, proceed to batch 2 if green
- 02:45 UTC: final batch complete, begin validation
- 03:10 UTC: handback to oncall for 30m observation
- 03:30 UTC: expected completion and status update

devops-bot: Reminder: ensure Dedicated customers with pinned regions have been notified individually — see list at https://docs.internal/redwood/dedicated-customers/eu-west1-list

Ava (support): i've prepared a slightly more empathetic customer notice for high-touch accounts: "We will be performing short maintenance that may temporarily affect request success rates. If this maintenance impacts your SLAs, please reply and we'll prioritize mitigation and rollback." approve?

Jamie (oncall): approved. add a direct line for enterprise accounts: enterprise-support@redwood.ai and ops escalation code 7.

Mateo: quick mitigation note: if we see KV cache warmup regress >10% after batch 2, route new requests to us-east1 by updating routing policy:
```
rdwctl routing set --region-preference us-east1 --weight 80 --reason "eu-west1 maintenance warmup regression"
```
Have rollback steps prepared.

Priya Rao: pre-window checklist complete except for one remaining item: confirm that the canary model is healthy in standby region. @Mateo can you confirm?

Mateo: canary looks green on test traffic. readiness probes passing.

ops-runner: scheduled automated status page updates: pre-window at 01:45 UTC, in-progress at 02:05 UTC, post-window at 03:35 UTC. all updates will include incident ticket INC-2026-0483.

Ava (support): copy for status page in-progress:
"Maintenance is in progress in eu-west1. We are performing rolling drains with minimal expected impact. Some requests may see short failures; our systems are failing over to healthy capacity. We'll post another update once maintenance is complete."

Jamie (oncall): final reminder: if customer biz-impact >SLA threshold, escalate to SRE lead (Priya then Jamie) and open exec-bridge. otherwise follow normal oncall runbook. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Scheduled automation: starting pre-window checks at 01:45 UTC.

Priya Rao: handoff note — i'll remain primary until 02:50 UTC. @Jamie will take over observation 02:50-03:30 and then return to standard rotation.

Ava (support): after windows are done, i'll post a brief postmortem-lite in the customer channel with impact summary and retries guidance.

Jamie (oncall): (post-window) maintenance complete at 03:28 UTC. observed a brief 0.9% 502 spike during batch 2 for ~4m, cache warmup took 7m longer than expected for one shard but traffic autoscaled and we did not need to reroute. status page updated and customer emails queued. closing INC-2026-0483 and marking as maintenance.

Mateo: noted — i'll follow up with a short RCA entry about cache warmup anomaly and consider increasing pre-warm threshold for future drains.

Ava (support): posted customer completion note and sent targeted notices to enterprise accounts. copied status page update: "Maintenance complete in eu-west1. Some requests experienced brief failures; normal service has resumed. If you continue to see issues, reply to this message or contact enterprise-support@redwood.ai."

Priya Rao: thanks team — nice work on the smooth roll. :party-parrot:
